added: Host a coop server right from an instance, no game menus needed. It loads the instance's mods and maps on its own, in the right order. Start it from the Worlds tab, hit Play to jump in as the host, and invite friends with their Steam ID or profile link.
The coop server's console shows up in the Logs tab while it runs.
The Worlds tab lists the servers you've played on, with how many people are on right now, the character you played there, and a Join button.
Characters you save in the game's character screen now show up in every instance, and the ones you delete stay deleted.
On Linux, lata can hide in the system tray when you close it too, on desktops that show tray icons.
A Characters page to make and tune your presets: look, clothes, profession and traits with the points in view, while your character walks around in 3D as you change things.
lata speaks Simplified Chinese (简体中文) and Russian (Русский) now. They're a first pass, so if something reads odd, tell us on Discord!
fixed: On Windows, a Java agent you add to an instance's Java arguments, like PZ Optimization's, loads instead of closing the game at once. typpy(Re.) on Discord found this one, thanks a lot!
On Windows, the tray icon looks sharp at any display scaling.

added: On Windows, lata can hide in the system tray when you close it. Turn on "Minimize to the system tray" in Settings; click the icon to bring it back, or quit from its menu.
Delete is in the sidebar's instance menu too.
changed: Delete shows in red in every instance menu.
The downloads pill shows a spinner until it knows the speed, so a download that just started doesn't look stuck.
If an instance can't be deleted yet, lata tells you why: the game is running, it's downloading, or mods are still going in.
fixed: Deleting an instance also clears the half download a cancelled install left, which could take about 10 GB for good.
A build lata can't clean up right away no longer makes deleting an instance fail; it goes next time.
If a Steam download server turns lata away, it tries the next one instead of failing the install.
A cancelled update keeps its half download, so trying again picks up where it stopped.
The downloads pill's fill stays inside its rounded ends at the start of a download.
The Workshop filters menu opens at the top, so "Game version" is always in view.
The can on the update screen keeps moving while an update downloads, so a slow download doesn't look stuck.
On Linux with a tiling window manager like Hyprland, the update screen shows as a small centered window instead of filling a tile.
A mod's pictures can't stand in for another mod's anymore: lata keeps each one under a name nobody can copy, and only trusts Steam's own picture hosts.

added: A Workshop tab: search Project Zomboid mods, sort them, filter by build and category, and leave categories out. Sign in with Steam and every mod shows who made it.
Each mod has its own page, with its description, pictures, changelog, the mods it needs and a button to install it.
Install a mod right from the Workshop: pick the instance, or make a new one and it only offers game versions the mod runs on.
Update or roll back just the mods you check, and filter the Mods tab to the ones with an update.
Sort mods by when you installed them or when they last updated. These two came from typpy(Re.) on Discord, thanks a lot!
View in Workshop in a mod's menu opens its page without leaving lata.
changed: The bar for checked mods floats over the list instead of pushing it up, and fits narrow windows.
Add is now Install everywhere, since that's what it does.
Instance menus are grouped: the instance, its files, copies of it, and Delete on its own at the end.

added: Pick any game version when you create an instance: choose a channel, then a version, the newest marked Latest. Older Build 42 releases like 42.20.4 are there too, for when an update breaks your save or your mods.
Packs keep the game at the version they were made on, so a friend gets the same game you played. Uncheck Keep the game at when exporting to follow the newest instead.
changed: The Discord button moved left, next to the library, giving the logo some room.
fixed: A pack can only ask for a game version lata knows, so it can't fill a shared game folder with the wrong files.

added: lata updates itself on Windows too, the same way it does on Linux.
Change version shows only the versions that run on your instance's game, and says what the others need.
About in Settings says whether a newer lata is out, and where to report a problem or find lata's folder.
changed: The update window has a line to read while it works, you can drag it around, and Skip for now shows up only when the download gets stuck.
On Windows, lata comes as a plain .exe: nothing to unzip.
Changing where your library lives opens right below, the drives coming in one after another.
Mod versions show the date and time where you are, not in UTC.
The logo's cross and eye have smooth edges.
fixed: The switch for automatic updates was squeezed out of sight in Settings.
Toast icons sit centered when there are two lines.

added: Duplicate an instance from its menu, mods and settings included.
Change a mod's version: go back to an older one when the newest breaks your save.
Undo a mod update with one click.
Java mods work: add ZombieBuddy to an instance and turn them on from its Mods tab.
A heads up when a mod you use has left the Workshop.
An About section in Settings, with the lata you're running.
This very list, after each update and in Settings whenever you want it.
A Discord button up top, to ask for help or say what broke.
changed: Game versions read like the game shows them (42.22.2) instead of Steam's build numbers, with the channel next to them: Stable or Pre-release.
Toasts got a new look, and some come with a button to act right there.
fixed: A download checks the drive has room before it starts, not halfway through.
Downloads keep going when your network changes, like hopping from Wi-Fi to cable.

added: The first lata you can try. Hi!
Several installs of the game side by side, each with its own game version, mods and saves.
Mods per instance: add them, turn them on or off, sort the load order, remove them.
Workshop mods and whole collections installed from a link, with the lata link browser extension.
Bring in the game you already play, worlds and mods included.
Share an instance as a pack, and open the ones your friends send.
Worlds, screenshots and live game logs for each instance.
Light and dark themes.
lata keeps itself up to date.
